subject: Capacity Surge Contention — 6-week benchmark + temporary term concessions
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Consideration to run competitor benchmark before renewal

Marissa / team,

Thanks for the renewal proposal. I wanted to flag that the product team has opened a benchmark with CloudSprint (their infra team reached out last week) — they are promising a 40% per-token cost reduction for our typical sessions and have offered a short pilot to prove throughput. Given our growth curve for Q4 we need to validate the numbers before approving the committed capacity.

Procurement (cc'd) will likely push for a trial/bake-off unless we can offer a short-term proof and clearer capacity guarantees. Happy to share technical profiles and sample payloads if that helps.

Can Redwood propose a structured benchmark window and any short-term term concessions to keep us moving toward a renewal? Also please confirm data residency and logging for the trial.

-Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of ML Platforms, Acme Retail
procurement@acmeretail.com

-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>; Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consideration to run competitor benchmark before renewal

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the heads up and for looping procurement. We take benchmarking concerns seriously and want to make this as low-friction as possible. Proposal below — attached is a short plan (acme_benchmark-plan-6wk.pdf) and a draft SOW with temporary terms (revised_sow_acme_redwood.docx).

High-level proposal:
- 6-week controlled benchmark window using your sample payloads (we'll mirror the CloudSprint parameters you shared).
- Dedicated capacity reservation for the trial (guaranteed steady-state throughput for the benchmark slices) so your performance numbers are reproducible.
- Temporary commercial concessions for the trial: 15% discount on usage during the 6-week window and a one-time credit if performance targets aren’t met.
- Technical guarantees: 99.5% request success rate, p95 latency target based on agreed SLAs for the sample session profile.
- Data residency: trial can be run in your preferred US region; logs available via secure export to your S3/KMS-protected bucket.

Ask: If you agree in principle we'll share the test harness and the doc link for signature. Would procurement prefer a narrower scope (3 weeks) or the full 6-week window?

Thanks — I’ve put Karthik on copy for technical specifics and Jordan for approvals if we need an exception to standard renewal terms.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: acme_benchmark-plan-6wk.pdf (pdf, 85KB), revised_sow_acme_redwood.docx (docx, 42KB)

-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmeretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consideration to run competitor benchmark before renewal

Sanjay — quick technical note from our side on the benchmark plan:
- We'll instrument exact workload replay with per-session KV caching enabled to mimic production caching patterns (this avoids a false negative on latency).
- For throughput, we'll provide a dedicated 4-GPU pool for the trial slice (NVIDIA H100-style profile).
- We'll expose token-level telemetry and tracing window mapped to your sample traces so you can reproduce results on your side.
- If you'd like, we can add a 48-hour preconditioning run to warm caches and KV; I recommend it for parity.

Also: the p95 numbers we propose are conservative; if the team wants tighter SLAs for the trial we can scope those into the SOW but they may change the temporary concession calculus.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

-----
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>; Maya Singh <maya@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consideration to run competitor benchmark before renewal

Thanks Marissa / Karthik — that all sounds reasonable. Two questions before we commit:
1) Data residency: can you confirm logs and telemetry stay within our US region for the duration and that the delivery to our S3 uses our KMS keys?
2) If Redwood outperforms CloudSprint during the 6-week window, what level of priority/commitment do we get for Q4 capacity (we're planning a 2x traffic increase).

Procurement wants the SOW language to be explicit on the credit trigger and on how a pass/fail decision is signed off. Maya — feel free to add if I missed anything.

-Sanjay

-----
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmeretail.com>; Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consideration to run competitor benchmark before renewal

Looping in approvals — I reviewed the proposed temporary concessions and am prepared to approve the 15% trial discount + up to a $50k one-time credit if targets are missed, subject to:
- A mutually agreed pass/fail criteria document in the SOW (we'll use the benchmark plan attachment as the base).
- A 60-day notice for any permanent capacity reservation beyond the trial (gives us time to provision dedicated pools).

Marissa, please confirm we can commit to the KMS/S3 delivery and that legal will accept the credit trigger language in the revised SOW. If procurement signs off, we can run the trial as early as next week.

Jordan Blake
VP, Revenue — Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

-----
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>; Maya Singh <maya@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T16:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consideration to run competitor benchmark before renewal

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement (Maya) reviewed the SOW and the benchmark plan — we have one small edit to the pass/fail window (requesting a 72-hour validation window post-trial to review outcomes). Otherwise Procurement is good.

Please send the DocuSign link for the revised SOW and we'll get this signed. If Redwood can confirm the S3/KMS routing in writing and the 60-day notice for capacity provisioning, we will pause the CloudSprint pilot.

I'll expect the DocuSign link and a confirmation email with the KMS routing note.

Thanks,
Sanjay

Attachments referenced earlier: acme_benchmark-plan-6wk.pdf, revised_sow_acme_redwood.docx
